issue.title: lib/model: Mark files below newly created symlinks as deleted (fixes #2571)

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
### Purpose

The scenario is well described in #2571, in short: If a dir is replaced by a symlink, the files within the dir aren't marked as deleted in the database if they exist at the location the new symlink points to. The other device will therefore fail to remove the directory because it isn't empty.  
The issue further describes that when you manually delete the directory, contents from the symlink target gets deleted: This isn't the case even previous to this PR, as we check that we don't descend into symlinks.

### Testing

New unit test for this scenario.

body:
This is mostly deliberate, as it's kind of hard to decide which errors mean the file doesn't exist. One typical case (that might be solved by your new stuff) is when a directory becomes a file, for example. Stat of the files inside the (previous) dir doesn't return NotExist.

Similarly, your test case (we lose permissions to a directory) means to me that we *should* propagate this as a delete, as it might be deliberate.

Deliberate or not it may still be wrong, so feel free to improve it. :)

> Similarly, your test case (we lose permissions to a directory) means to me that we should propagate this as a delete, as it might be deliberate.

I guess that's the only thing to be discussed then, because if this is to be expected, this bug report is invalid. For me it is unexpected that something gets deleted when it becomes unavailable for any other reason than being deleted (e.g. permissions changed), and thus falls under our 1. goal against data loss. I tried to find arguments, but I don't have any. It just feels wrong to "delete" files by changing permissions: In my opinion changing permissions should prevent Syncthing from accessing something, but isn't simultaneously a sign to get rid of it...

Well I can agree with that. Question then is just how to handle it. I think we were discussing somewhere else what do about scanning errors; currently they're sort of invisible. And we need to make sure we cover stuff like dir-to-file conversions, which you're already on top of.

Hi, I absolutely agree with the OP, it's tragic when something goes wrong and a mass of files is unintentionally deleted. Been there, done that, got the t-shirt....
I would suggest a modal popup message before syncing say anything over 100 recognised deletions asking user to confirm before deleting. Yes I know that might be inconvenient in some instances, but honestly wayyyy less inconvenient than say an entire direcory being deleted due to user error....
Thanks, guys, love syncthing it's the best bar none. I have 1363449folders   93891dirs   ~20292GB being synced perfectly across 2 Synologies... Cheers!!!
If you're go for changing stuff there, please mind the "Case-only renames" mess (https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/issues/1787). Fast case-renames caused unwanted deletes few times for me.
We don't have enough people solving the problems, yet we have more than enough project managers telling what needs to be solved.

Hey, I'm not telling anyone what needs to be solved and what isn't. 
Obviously I'm not in any position to do such a thing.
The great majority of work here done by only few core contributors, to whom I'm very thankful.

I occasionally chime in to give some feedback and/or rise a point I consider relevant. I apologize if you find my comment opposite of helpful. You are free to ignore my input as you like.

Code fixing this would have close to no overlap with an code fixing case only renames, so I am not sure "hey while you're at it - fix this too" is useful input.

The only thing this has with case only renames is the fact that the end result is the same - which is under some circumstances files end up deleted.

We are well aware of what the annoying pain points are, so no need to cross reference and convolute issues and give pointers what we should fix, same way like you did in #4551.

issue.title: lib/model, lib/scanner: More precise deletion detection (fixes #2571, fixes #4573)

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
### Purpose

Fixes #2571 and #4573 by extending the file info returned from a scan by a "ReplacedDir" parameter, which signifies that the old file info in the db was a directory (and now is a file/symlink). This information is used to detect deleted children, for which "IsNotExist" returns false.  
In addition this makes sure that these deleted children are updated in the db before their parent is replaced, thus preventing intermediate pull (dir not empty) failures when the entire update exceeds the batch size.  
Compared to #4568 (which is obsolete if going forward with the approach of this PR) this uses information from scanning instead of doing more lstat calls.

### Testing

Two unit tests specific to the fixed issues and `TestInternalScan`. The last one is there because all tests passed with an earlier version of this PR, while it was severely broken - this test would have failed.

issue.body:
This reverts commit 6d3f9d5154b4c6b39f8083255cc9ed36b5c51146 / #4584.

In the presence of both case sensitive and insensitive systems this is seriously flawed, see #4756 and https://forum.syncthing.net/t/files-deleted-after-update-to-v0-14-45-rc-2/11282/19. Admittedly there is now evidence for that, but circumstances and Occam's razor point to it.

This undos the fixes for #2571 and #4573.

body: Sorry to jump in here, but I wanted to add another situation where this is problematic.  Say, for instance, that there is an I/O error while trying to Lstat() a file (perhaps filesystem corruption or failing hard drive?).  Now, syncthing is going to delete the good copy of the file from the remote.

There's a handful of very specific error codes that should probably not be treated as deletion, namely whatever the Go equivalents are to EIO, ESTALE, EAGAIN, all of which aren't indicative of the file being gone, just not being accessible for reasons other than permissions (I do agree that lack of access permissions makes sense to trigger deletion though).
This is already solved, see #4765. It will not remove anything unless we know for sure it has been deleted (parent is file/symlink or IsNotExist from Go's os package is true).
